items.title: Call to Meditation
items.text: “Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the Lord!”

lines.text: Oh come, let us sing to the Lord; let us make a joyful noise to the rock of our salvation! Let us come into his presence with thanksgiving; let us make a joyful noise to him with songs of praise! For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
Oh come, let us worship and bow down; let us kneel before the Lord, our Maker! For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.

items.title: Prayer of Invocation & The Lord’s Prayer
items.text: Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy Name. Thy Kingdom come, thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors. Lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil. For thine is the kingdom, the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.

lines.text: Oh give thanks to the Lord, for he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever! Let the redeemed of the Lord say so, whom he has redeemed from trouble and gathered in from the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the south. Some wandered in desert wastes, finding no way to a city to dwell in; hungry and thirsty, their soul fainted within them.
Then they cried to the Lord in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.
He led them by a straight way till they reached a city to dwell in.
Let them thank the Lord for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of man!
For he satisfies the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills with good things. Some sat in darkness and in the shadow of death.
Then they cried to the Lord in their trouble, and he delivered them from their distress.
He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, and burst their bonds apart.
Let them thank the Lord for his steadfast love, for his wondrous works to the children of man! And let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving, and tell of his deeds in songs of joy!

items.title: Congregational Response
items.piece: In Thanksgiving Let Us Praise Him

items.title: Corporate Prayer of Confession
items.text: God, our heavenly Father, You are our Creator, Redeemer, and Sustainer. Every good and perfect gift comes from You. Yet we confess that we have doubted Your generous heart which delights to give what is good to Your children. We have murmured and complained against You. We have failed to give thanks to You in all circumstances. Empower us to cast off these and all other sins of our heart knowing that they are an affront and insult to You. Fill us anew with Your Spirit and deepen our gratitude so that we might serve and obey You with undivided and joyful hearts.

items.title: Assurance of Divine Pardon
items.text: “For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sake he became poor, so that you by his poverty might become rich.”

items.title: Gloria Patri
items.text: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son: and to the Holy Ghost; As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be: world without end. Amen.

items.title: Profession of Faith
items.text: I believe in God, the Father almighty, Maker of heaven and earth, and in Jesus Christ, his only Son, our Lord, who was conceived by the Holy Ghost, born of the Virgin Mary, suffered under Pontius Pilate, was crucified, dead and buried; he descended into hell; the third day he rose again from the dead; he ascended into heaven, and sitteth on the right hand of God the Father Almighty; from thence he shall come to judge the quick and the dead. I believe in the Holy Ghost, the holy catholic* Church, the communion of saints, the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the body, and the life everlasting. Amen.
items.creed_note: *that is, the true Christian church of all times and all places

items.title: The Giving of Tithes and Offerings
The Doxology and Prayer of Dedication
items.text: Praise God, from whom all blessings flow; Praise Him, all creatures here below; Praise Him above, ye heavenly host; Praise Father, Son, and Holy Ghost. Amen.

lines.text: All flesh is grass, and all its beauty is like the flower of the field;
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the Word of our God will stand forever. Amen.

notes.label: Call to Worship
notes.text: We are summoned to worship by God’s word, calling His people into His presence to honor Him in spirit and truth, opening a sacred conversation that unfolds throughout the service. We sing in response to God’s call to worship, which is a reminder that worship is at God’s initiative, not ours.

notes.label: Come, Ye Thankful People, Come
notes.text: Written in 1844 by English clergyman and hymnwriter Henry Alford, this hymn blends the physical gratitude of an autumn harvest with the spiritual anticipation of Christ’s return. While the first verse celebrates the gathering of earthly crops, the final verses are looking forward to the great final harvest when God will gather His people into His eternal home.

notes.label: Corporate Confession
notes.text: God graciously reveals His holiness, and His people respond with humble confession, trusting His promise of forgiveness in Christ.

notes.label: dGroup
notes.text: A group of 3-5, same gender individuals, led by a trained disciple-maker, that meets regularly to encourage one another as Christ-followers to continue taking steps in becoming a disciple of Christ who makes other disciples.

notes.label: Children’s Church
notes.text: Children ages 4 up to 4th grade are invited to come forward and exit out the side door for Children’s Church. Following the worship service, they may be picked up in the Fellowship Hall.

sermon.title: Spiritual Renewal: Resting in the Lord
intro: In Nehemiah 4, we discover the moment God’s people begin making progress in their mission, opposition begins to intensify. As we have established, the rebuilding of Jerusalem was more than a construction project, it was part of God’s larger work of the spiritual renewal of His people after the exile. Sometimes we mistakenly assume that if we are doing what God wants us to do, everything ought to go smoothly and we will experience great success. But Scripture teaches us something different. Faithfulness does not exempt us from difficulty. Obedience does not guarantee an absence of opposition. Spiritual renewal does not mean the absence of spiritual conflict. However, we can interpret danger in light of the power and promises of God. That is the good news of Nehemiah 4. God’s people can persevere and rest in the Lord because their confidence is not ultimately in themselves, but in the Lord who fights for them. We see three things in this chapter that enable us to rest in the Lord.

points.heading: II. REMEMBER
points.quote: Psalm 27:14 — “Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!”

points.heading: III. TRUST
sub: Exodus 14:14 — “The LORD will fight for you.”
